title: Canonical naive cotangent functor with fixed base and prescribed maps
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\operatorname{CAlg}_R$ be its category of commutative algebras. For an $R$-algebra $T$, use the canonical presentation $R[T]\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and its augmentation ideal $I_T$. Define $N_R(T)$ to be the canonical naive cotangent complex [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], restricted to $R$-modules, with $I_T/I_T^2$ in degree $-1$ and $\bigoplus_{t\in T}T\,\mathrm d[t]$ in degree $0$, zero elsewhere, and differential $[g]\mapsto\sum_t\gamma_T(\partial g/\partial[t])\mathrm d[t]$. Cochain complexes and chain maps are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $u:T\to T'$ let $u_\sharp:R[T]\to R[T']$ fix coefficients and send $[t]$ to $[u(t)]$. It carries $I_T$ into $I_{T'}$; define the degree-minus-one map by $[g]\mapsto[u_\sharp(g)]$ and the degree-zero map by $a\,\mathrm d[t]\mapsto u(a)\,\mathrm d[u(t)]$, with coefficients added when variable labels collide. These maps commute with the displayed differential and preserve identities and compositions, defining the functor $N_R:\operatorname{CAlg}_R\to\operatorname{CoCh}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$. Use the existing ideal conormal quotient and polynomial differential basis; the two-term complex may equivalently be formed by the existing mapping cone of its differential between degree-zero single complexes, with the canonical biproduct-with-zero coordinate identifications.
